subject.title: fix: discord exec approvals fails against local self-signed TLS gateway

question: Should maintainers repair/review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80204 as the shared bootstrap TLS fingerprint fix, replace it with a clean equivalent, or hold for broader TLS pin precedence review?
rationale: The remaining fix changes certificate fingerprint trust routing for Gateway clients, and the active branch is conflicting, so maintainer security-boundary intent is needed before landing.

options.title: Repair and review active PR
options.body: Resolve the open PR conflicts/import drift and validate local, remote, env, CLI, and non-WSS TLS fingerprint semantics on the actual merged tree.

options.title: Replace with a clean successor
options.body: Open a narrow equivalent replacement if the active branch is not worth reconciling while preserving its shared-bootstrap fix intent.

options.title: Hold for TLS policy review
options.body: Keep this issue open without landing until maintainers revisit TLS pin precedence across local, remote, CLI, and env targets.

recommendation.title: Repair and review active PR
recommendation.body: Resolve the open PR conflicts/import drift and validate local, remote, env, CLI, and non-WSS TLS fingerprint semantics on the actual merged tree.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is prior ownership of Gateway TLS fingerprint support and shared approval/bootstrap helpers.
